problem: The heading 'Protocol: two qubits, two bits, one state' miscounts the qubits. The protocol needs three qubits: the unknown qubit q0, Alice's half of the Bell pair q1 and Bob's half q2. The body of the section itself says 'Label the three qubits q0, q1 and q2', so the heading contradicts it and a student revising from headings will get the resource count wrong.
fix: Rename the heading to 'Protocol: three qubits, two bits, one state' (or 'One unknown qubit, one Bell pair, two classical bits').

problem: Writing |Ψ₀⟩ = (α|0⟩ + β|1⟩) ⊗ (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2 puts the 1/√2 outside the tensor product, so it can be read as dividing the whole product, or as not dividing the second factor. The normalisation is ambiguous on first reading.
fix: Write |Ψ₀⟩ = (α|0⟩ + β|1⟩) ⊗ [(|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2], so it is clear the 1/√2 normalises only the Bell pair.

problem: The traps switch between correct statements ('Do not say teleportation copies |ψ⟩', 'Bob needs both classical bits') and bare errors ('Mix-up the corrections', 'Forget that the Bell pair is consumed'). The two forms read differently, and 'Mix-up the corrections' can look like advice to mix them up.
fix: Phrase every trap as the mistake to avoid: 'Do not mix up the corrections: 01 needs X, 10 needs Z, 11 needs XZ (Z then X, a global minus sign is allowed).' and 'Do not forget that the Bell pair is consumed: one teleportation uses one shared Bell pair and two classical bits.'
